tasks.title: Implement the .todos.json store in src/store.js with its temp-dir tests
tasks.description: Create src/store.js, a dependency-free (node:fs only) persistence layer for todos, together with its own node:test suite. Every function takes a `dir` argument that defaults to process.cwd(), so the suite can point it at a temporary directory and never read or write the project's own .todos.json. Throwing on an unknown id keeps the CLI simple: the CLI turns the thrown Error into exit code 1 and a stderr message.

context.reason: confirms "type": "module" and that tests run under node:test
the existing node:test style (test + assert/strict) this new suite follows

edits.change:
Write src/store.js using only node:fs and node:path. Exports: `const DATA_FILE = '.todos.json'`; a non-exported `dataPath(dir)` returning `path.join(dir, DATA_FILE)`; and these named exports:
- `readTodos(dir = process.cwd())` — if the file does not exist return []; otherwise JSON.parse the contents and return only entries that are objects with a numeric `id` and a string `text`; wrap JSON.parse in try/catch and rethrow as `new Error('could not parse .todos.json: ' + err.message)`.
- `writeTodos(todos, dir = process.cwd())` — `fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` then `fs.writeFileSync(dataPath(dir), JSON.stringify(todos, null, 2) + '\n')`.
- `addTodo(text, dir = process.cwd())` — trim text; if it is empty throw `new Error('todo text cannot be empty')`; read todos; newId is 1 when the list is empty or its maximum id is 0, otherwise the maximum id + 1; create `{ id: newId, text, done: false, createdAt: new Date().toISOString() }`, append, writeTodos, return the new record.
- `listTodos({ dir = process.cwd(), pendingOnly = false } = {})` — read todos and return `pendingOnly ? todos.filter(t => !t.done) : todos`.
- `completeTodo(id, dir = process.cwd())` — read todos, find the entry whose id strictly equals `Number(id)` via a shared non-exported `findById(todos, id)` helper, throw `new Error('no todo with id: ' + id)` when absent, set `todo.done = true`, writeTodos, return the updated record.
- `removeTodo(id, dir = process.cwd())` — same lookup, throw the same `no todo with id: <id>` error when absent, filter the entry out, writeTodos, return the removed record.
No console output and no process.exit in this file.

Write test/store.test.js. Imports: `import { test } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, `import fs from 'node:fs'`, `import os from 'node:os'`, `import path from 'node:path'`, and `{ readTodos, writeTodos, addTodo, listTodos, completeTodo, removeTodo }` from '../src/store.js'. Create the temp dir once at module load with `const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'todo-store-'))` and register `test.after(() => fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }))`. Never reference the repository root or the project's .todos.json. Tests:
- `addTodo` returns `{ id: 1, text: 'buy milk', done: false }` with a string createdAt, and a second add returns id 2.
- `addTodo` throws /todo text cannot be empty/ for '   ' and leaves the stored list empty.
- `listTodos({ dir, pendingOnly: true })` returns only the pending entries after `completeTodo(1, dir)`.
- `completeTodo` returns the same id with done set to true, and that flag is true in the file too.
- `completeTodo(99, dir)` and `removeTodo(99, dir)` both throw /no todo with id: 99/.
- `removeTodo` deletes the record and leaves other ids untouched; ids are not renumbered (after removing id 1, `addTodo` returns 3).
- `readTodos` returns [] for a directory with no .todos.json, and `writeTodos` creates the directory when it is missing.
- `writeTodos` + `readTodos` round-trip a record with `done: true` and `createdAt: '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'`.
- `readTodos` throws /could not parse .todos.json/ when the file contains `{` (use a sub-temp-dir created inside that test).

tasks.title: Implement add/list/done/remove plus --pending and --dir in src/cli.js, with temp-dir tests
tasks.description: Create src/cli.js, the argument parser and command dispatcher, together with its node:test suite. It reaches the filesystem only through src/store.js, so the whole CLI can be driven from a test with a temp directory passed via --dir. run() returns { exitCode, stdout, stderr } rather than calling process.exit, which is what makes it testable.

context.reason: the data-access module this task's cli.js imports from (addTodo, listTodos, completeTodo, removeTodo)
the node:test conventions these new suites match

edits.change:
Write src/cli.js importing `node:path` and the named exports `addTodo, listTodos, completeTodo, removeTodo` from './store.js'. Exports:
- `export const USAGE` — a multi-line template string whose first line is exactly `Usage: todo <command> [options]`, followed by the commands `add <text>`, `list`, `done <id>`, `remove <id>`, `help`, the options `--pending   only show todos that are not done` and `--dir <path>  read and write .todos.json in <path> (default: current directory)`, and the line `Todos are stored in .todos.json.`.
- `export function parseArgs(argv)` — iterate argv with a for loop building `{ command: null, positional: [], flags: {} }`; `--pending` sets flags.pending = true and continues; `--dir` consumes argv[i + 1] as flags.dir (falling back to '.' when there is no next argument) and skips it; any other `--name` token becomes a flag whose value is the next argument when one exists and does not start with '--', otherwise true, consuming that argument when used; a non-flag token becomes `command` when command is still null, otherwise is pushed onto positional. Return the object.
- `export function run(argv = [])` — build `const out = []`, `const err = []` and a `fail(message)` helper that pushes to err and returns `{ exitCode: 1, stdout: out.join('\n'), stderr: err.join('\n') }`. Call parseArgs; set `const dir = path.resolve(flags.dir || process.cwd())`; wrap the command dispatch in try/catch and return fail(err.message) from the catch.
  - add: if positional.join(' ') is blank, return fail('todo text cannot be empty'); otherwise `const todo = addTodo(positional.join(' '), dir)` and push `Added ${todo.id}: ${todo.text}`.
  - list: `const todos = listTodos({ dir, pendingOnly: Boolean(flags.pending) })`; if empty push 'No todos.'; otherwise for each todo push `${t.id} [${t.done ? 'x' : ' '}] ${t.text}`, then push an empty string, then `${todos.length} todos`, and when at least one is done push `${doneCount} done`.
  - done: if positional[0] is undefined return fail('usage: todo done <id>'); otherwise `const todo = completeTodo(positional[0], dir)` and push `Done ${todo.id}: ${todo.text}`.
  - remove: if positional[0] is undefined return fail('usage: todo remove <id>'); otherwise `const todo = removeTodo(positional[0], dir)` and push `Removed ${todo.id}: ${todo.text}`.
  - help: push USAGE. default: push USAGE and return exitCode 1 with empty stderr.
  Append one trailing newline to stdout when any line was pushed, so `run(['list'])` with a single pending todo returns exactly '1 [ ] buy milk\n\n1 todos\n'. On success return `{ exitCode: 0, stdout: out.join('\n'), stderr: '' }`.
Neither run() nor parseArgs() may call process.exit or write to the console.

Write test/cli.test.js. Imports: `import { test } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, `import fs from 'node:fs'`, `import os from 'node:os'`, `import path from 'node:path'`, `{ parseArgs, run }` from '../src/cli.js' and `{ readTodos }` from '../src/store.js'. Create the temp dir once at module load with `const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'todo-cli-'))`, register `test.after(() => fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }))`, and define `const cli = (...argv) => run([...argv, '--dir', dir])` so every call targets the temp directory. Use nested `test()` groups 'parseArgs' and 'commands'. Tests:
- parseArgs(['add', 'buy', 'milk']) returns command 'add', positional ['buy', 'milk'], no dir flag; parseArgs(['list', '--pending']) sets flags.pending true; parseArgs(['list', '--dir', '/tmp/x']) sets flags.dir '/tmp/x'.
- add then list: `cli('add', 'buy milk')` and `cli('add', 'walk dog')` exit 0 and report ids 1 and 2; `cli('list')` stdout is exactly '1 [ ] buy milk\n2 [ ] walk dog\n\n2 todos\n'.
- after `cli('done', '1')`, `cli('list')` includes '1 [x] buy milk' and ends with '2 todos\n1 done\n'; `cli('list', '--pending')` includes '2 [ ] walk dog' and does not include 'buy milk'.
- `cli('remove', '2')` then `cli('list')` includes '1 todos' and no 'walk dog'.
- `cli('done', '99')` and `cli('remove', '99')` exit 1 with /no todo with id/ in stderr; `cli('add')` exits 1 with /todo text cannot be empty/.
- on the empty temp dir `cli('list')` stdout is exactly 'No todos.\n'.
- `cli('help')` exits 0 and prints 'Usage:'; `cli('bogus')` and `run([])` both exit 1.
- the temp `.todos.json` really holds the record: after `cli('add', 'x')`, `readTodos(dir)[0]` deep-equals `{ id: 1, text: 'x', done: false }` with a string createdAt.

contracts.statement: src/store.js exports named functions `readTodos(dir = process.cwd())`, `writeTodos(todos, dir = process.cwd())`, `addTodo(text, dir = process.cwd())`, `listTodos({ dir = process.cwd(), pendingOnly = false } = {})`, `completeTodo(id, dir = process.cwd())` and `removeTodo(id, dir = process.cwd())`. Every one resolves the data file as `path.join(dir, '.todos.json')`, so a caller that passes a temp directory never reads or writes the project's own `.todos.json`. `completeTodo` and `removeTodo` throw an `Error` whose message is exactly `no todo with id: <id>` when that id is absent; `addTodo` throws an `Error` whose message is exactly `todo text cannot be empty` for empty or whitespace-only text.

A todo record is `{ id: number, text: string, done: boolean, createdAt: string }`, where `id` is a 1-based integer assigned as `max(existing ids, defaulting to 0) + 1` and `createdAt` is an ISO-8601 string from `new Date().toISOString()`. `readTodos` returns `[]` when `.todos.json` does not exist; when it exists it returns the parsed array filtered to objects having a numeric `id` and a string `text`; when the file contains malformed JSON it throws an `Error` whose message starts with ``could not parse `.todos.json`: ``. `writeTodos` writes `JSON.stringify(todos, null, 2)` followed by one trailing newline, creating `dir` with `fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` when it is missing.

src/cli.js exports named functions `parseArgs(argv)`, `run(argv)` and the constant `USAGE`. `parseArgs` returns `{ command, positional, flags }` where `command` is the first non-flag argument (or `null`), `positional` holds the remaining arguments after the command, and `flags` maps each `--name` to its value. Only two flags exist: `--pending` (boolean, never takes a value) and `--dir <path>` (the data directory, defaulting to `process.cwd()`). `run(argv)` returns `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }`, and never calls process.exit or writes to the real console, so tests call it directly. Commands: `add <text...>` joins the remaining arguments with single spaces and prints `Added <id>: <text>`; `list` prints one line per todo as `<id> [<x| >] <text>`, then a blank line, then the total count as `N todos`, then a comma-separated `K done` line only when K > 0, and prints the literal line `No todos.` when the list is empty; `done <id>` marks the todo and prints `Done <id>: <text>`; `remove <id>` prints `Removed <id>: <text>`; `help` prints `USAGE` (whose first line is `Usage: todo <command> [options]`) with exitCode 0; an unknown or missing command prints `USAGE` to stdout with exitCode 1.
